args.text: [lane-otter] Risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale answers send users to old or dead servers after a site moves or fails over. (2) Slow recovery: fixes such as changing addresses during an outage take longer to reach users. (3) Poisoned or hijacked answers stay in the cache longer, so harm lasts longer.

[lane-otter] Idempotent (safe to repeat) retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave you unsure whether a request worked, so you must be able to send it again. If repeating changes nothing beyond the first success, you avoid double charges, duplicate orders and other harm.

[lane-otter] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (a time-ordered unique identifier) as a primary key: (1) It leaks creation time, since the first part of the key holds a timestamp, so outsiders can estimate when a record was made. (2) Keys are larger than a plain whole-number key (16 bytes against 4 or 8), so indexes take more space, though time ordering keeps inserts friendlier than random UUIDs.

[lane-otter] A write-ahead log (a file where each change is written down before it is applied to the main data) lets a database recover after a crash by replaying the saved changes. It also makes writes faster and safer, because adding to the end of a log is quicker than updating many places in the main data straight away.

[lane-otter] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: a newer client may change speed or behaviour on its own, so results from different runs would no longer be comparable. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the same test later and get the same setup, which makes surprising results easier to investigate.
